 Warriors’ Quinten Post trade idea echoes painful Gary Payton II saga 
 They can't do this surely... By Peter O'Keefe | Oct 24, 2026, 12:35 AM EDT Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Golden State Warriors, Quinten Post. Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images | Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images Quinten Post only departed the Golden State Warriors this past offseason, but already there's a suggestion that the front office could reunite with the seven-footer in a deal with the Memphis Grizzlies.
--> Quinten Post only departed the Golden State Warriors this past offseason, but already there's a suggestion that the front office could reunite with the seven-footer in a deal with the Memphis Grizzlies.
 In a move that would echo the entire Gary Payton II saga four years ago, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints has referred to the Grizzlies holding a $28.8 million traded player exception they could use to absorb Porzingis' contract if they're motivated with the necessary draft capital.
--> In a move that would echo the entire Gary Payton II saga four years ago, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints has referred to the Grizzlies holding a $28.8 million traded player exception they could use to absorb Porzingis' contract if they're motivated with the necessary draft capital.
 Quinten Post trade idea echoes Gary Payton II saga
--> Quinten Post trade idea echoes Gary Payton II saga
 Siegel has suggested the Warriors flip Porzingis for Post in a deal that would simply be correcting their free agency decision during the offseason. Golden State signed Porzingis to a two-year, $40 million extension prior to free agency, before choosing not to match the three-year, $30 million offer sheet the Grizzlies gave to Post.
--> Siegel has suggested the Warriors flip Porzingis for Post in a deal that would simply be correcting their free agency decision during the offseason. Golden State signed Porzingis to a two-year, $40 million extension prior to free agency, before choosing not to match the three-year, $30 million offer sheet the Grizzlies gave to Post.
 The idea of making such a move to essentially address an offseason mistake is rather painful, particularly when it would likely take a first-round pick in order to achieve it. The Warriors could have simply let Porzingis walk and re-signed Post, potentially to a deal that was less than what the Grizzlies ultimately offered as a restricted free agent.
--> The idea of making such a move to essentially address an offseason mistake is rather painful, particularly when it would likely take a first-round pick in order to achieve it. The Warriors could have simply let Porzingis walk and re-signed Post, potentially to a deal that was less than what the Grizzlies ultimately offered as a restricted free agent.
 Would Golden State really want to sacrifice draft capital to fix their own error? That seems like a tough pill to swallow and is why this kind of trade should be deemed unlikely, particularly when Post isn't a starting quality player that they can just plug into the opening five.
--> Would Golden State really want to sacrifice draft capital to fix their own error? That seems like a tough pill to swallow and is why this kind of trade should be deemed unlikely, particularly when Post isn't a starting quality player that they can just plug into the opening five.
 One scenario I am keeping an eye on is the Grizzlies.
Memphis owns a $28.8M TPE, and sources told @ClutchPoints they will be very open to utilizing this TPE to take on bad contracts for draft compensation.
Could this lead to a Porzingis-Quinten Post swap? https://t.co/yfDhoCv4Ww 
— Brett Siegel (@BrettSiegelNBA) October 23, 2026 They do have a history of making such a deal though. The Warriors let Payton walk to the Portland Trail Blazers as a free agent after the 2022 NBA championship, before reacquiring him in a five-team trade that saw them send out former second overall pick James Wiseman at the following mid-season deadline.
--> They do have a history of making such a deal though. The Warriors let Payton walk to the Portland Trail Blazers as a free agent after the 2022 NBA championship, before reacquiring him in a five-team trade that saw them send out former second overall pick James Wiseman at the following mid-season deadline.
 Warriors need to find an upgrade at center in Kristaps Porzingis trade
--> Warriors need to find an upgrade at center in Kristaps Porzingis trade
 Flipping Porzingis for Post, regardless of what draft capital is involved and the luxury tax savings, would be a step backwards. That's nothing against Post who Golden State would love to have right now given their diminished center rotation, but they need a better option than what the Dutchman can deliver.
--> Flipping Porzingis for Post, regardless of what draft capital is involved and the luxury tax savings, would be a step backwards. That's nothing against Post who Golden State would love to have right now given their diminished center rotation, but they need a better option than what the Dutchman can deliver.
 There are some starting quality centers making less than Porzingis' $20 million, but most options that would be considered a serious 'upgrade' make more and would require an additional contract or potentially two.
--> There are some starting quality centers making less than Porzingis' $20 million, but most options that would be considered a serious 'upgrade' make more and would require an additional contract or potentially two.
 The Grizzlies' TPE should still be of interest as a team who could absorb Porzingis' contract, but the Warriors should only be exploring that as a third team that lands them a quality big from another team.
